explanation: A count of the population of Israel, carried out to organize and administer the tribes.
The transfer of property, status, or rights from one generation to the next within a family or tribe.
The twelve groups that made up the people of Israel, each with its own leader and territory, descended from Jacob's twelve sons.
One of the twelve spies whom Moses sent to explore Canaan; he and Joshua were the only ones who believed that Israel could conquer the land.
A key figure in Numbers, who succeeded Moses as leader of the Israelites and led them into the promised land of Canaan.
Men who fought in the army and took part in military battles to protect and expand Israel's territory.
A female offspring, mentioned especially in this book because the daughters of Zelophehad were granted the right to inherit.
